records.best_practice: Lock out, tag out AND ground every high-voltage circuit before working on it — grounding is the only protection that works if someone energizes the circuit by mistake. Test substation protective devices mechanically as well as electrically: a trip circuit that sounds correct may not actually open the breaker. Verify the mine communication system regularly.

records.best_practice: Build seals to withstand the explosive forces that can develop behind them — the MINER Act raised the standard to 50 psi and later 120 psi as a direct result of Sago. Monitor the atmosphere behind seals for methane accumulation. Store additional SCSRs along all escapeways and verify their functionality. Provide post-accident wireless communication and tracking systems. Ensure mine rescue teams can reach the mine within one hour.

records.mine: Aracoma Alma Mine No. 1 / Aracoma Coal Company (Massey Energy)
records.best_practice: Maintain all stoppings and ventilation controls that separate belt entries from designated escapeways — a single missing stopping can fill the escapeway with smoke. Install and maintain fire detection and suppression systems on all belt conveyors. Install directional lifelines along every escapeway so miners can navigate in zero visibility. During evacuation in dense smoke, maintain continuous physical contact with the crew and never separate from the group.

records.mine: Darby Mine No. 1 / Kentucky Darby LLC
records.best_practice: Before any flame cutting or welding near a seal, test for methane in every area that could be affected — including inside the sealed area itself. A low reading in the entry tells you nothing about the atmosphere behind the seal. Build and verify seals to federal specifications. Train miners never to remove the SCSR mouthpiece to communicate during evacuation — use hand signals or written notes instead. Eliminate hot work near seals wherever an alternative method exists.

records.best_practice: Implement an annual structural inspection program for all surface bins, hoppers, and support structures, especially those exposed to corrosive materials. Follow up on engineering consultant recommendations within specified timelines. Measure shear tab thickness and connection integrity at scheduled intervals. Do not allow vehicles or personnel to position under bins without confirming structural integrity. Dismantle and replace severely corroded structures before returning to service.

records.best_practice: Maintain incombustible content (rock dust) at required levels throughout the mine — this is the last barrier that stops a local methane ignition from becoming a mine-wide coal dust explosion. Inspect shearer bits before every cut and replace worn or broken bits. Verify that every water spray on the shearer is clear and functioning. Provide ventilation sufficient to dilute and carry away methane at the face. Never maintain a second set of books or give advance warning of inspections — concealment does not remove hazards, it accumulates them. Protect miners who report safety concerns from retaliation.

Provide ventilation sufficient to dilute and carry away methane at the face. Never maintain a second set of books or give advance warning of inspections — concealment does not remove hazards, it accumulates them. Protect miners who report safety concerns from retaliation.

records.best_practice: Review and follow site specific blast plan prior to loading any explosives. Utilize technology, such as face profilers and borehole probes, to obtain specific geometric details of the material to be blasted. Adjust stemming depth and/or decking to maintain adequate burden on all sections of the blast hole. Develop a drill pattern by considering geology, face geometry, and surface topography. Clear and remove all persons from the blast area unless suitable blasting shelters are provided to protect persons from flyrock. Allow at least 15 seconds after a blast for any flyrock to drop. Examine blast site geology, communicate with the driller and review the drill log for angles, voids, competency of rock, loss of air, etc., prior to the loading any explosives. Make appropriate adjustments to ensure that the holes are not overloaded. Ensure blasting and fly rock areas are properly calculated to ensure the blast site is clear of all persons. Determine the actual burden for all face holes along their length and adjust the explosive power factor along the borehole accordingly.

records.best_practice: Never place metallic material of any kind around a miner wearable component — shielding the MWC completely defeats the proximity detection system and the machine will not stop. Wear the MWC on the chest area, unobscured by pouches, belts, or other equipment, exactly as the manufacturer specifies. Conduct both static measurements and dynamic tests of the PDS at the start of every shift, including verification that all machine-mounted drivers illuminate. Install the machine-mounted locator option so the PDS detects a malfunctioning driver and prevents machine movement.

records.best_practice: Block longwall shields against hazardous motion before performing maintenance or electrical work. Be aware of pinch points around hydraulic components of longwall shields. Properly train miners who install or maintain shields on the hazards of unblocked shields. Maintain clear communication while performing work near or on longwall shields. Never position yourself between the shield and adjacent structure unless it is properly blocked.

records.best_practice: De-energize, lock-out, tag-out, and block machinery against motion before performing repairs or maintenance. Provide and ensure proper use of fall protection where there is a danger of falling, with a suitable fall arrest connection and secure anchorage. records.best_practice: De-energize, lock out, tag out, and block belt conveyors against hazardous motion before performing repairs or maintenance. Provide proper platforms, walkways, deck-level access or personnel lifts that allow safe access to elevated components. Install and maintain belt wipers to remove material from belts.
